🧠 Crypto News Brief: Institutional crypto keeps building even as risk appetite stays cautious — Wall Street pushes deeper into ETH and SOL, capital rotates out of Bitcoin ETFs, and Washington races the clock on market-structure rules. 🏦 Morgan Stanley Expands Crypto Lineup With Staking Ether & Solana ETPs Morgan Stanley Investment Management listed the Morgan Stanley Ethereum Trust (MSSE) and Morgan Stanley Solana Trust (MSOL) on NYSE Arca, each charging a 0.14% fee and passing all staking rewards through to investors. The launch extends the firm's crypto ETP suite past $14 billion in assets, following its earlier Bitcoin Trust and a push into spot trading on E*TRADE. Read full story 📜 SEC Chair Backs CLARITY Act, Warns Agency Will Act Alone If Congress Stalls SEC Chair Paul Atkins pledged technical support to help Congress pass the CLARITY Act before the Senate's August recess, while telling CNBC the agency is ready to issue its own crypto market-structure rules if lawmakers fail to act. The bill still faces unresolved Democratic concerns over ethics provisions tied to the President's crypto interests. More details 🔄 Bitcoin ETFs Bleed for a Fourth Day as Ethereum Funds Keep Winning US spot Bitcoin ETFs shed roughly 3,170 BTC (about $200M) over the past week, led by outflows from BlackRock's IBIT, while Ethereum ETFs pulled in 37,959 ETH for a third straight weekly gain, with BlackRock's ETHA driving most of that demand. Analysts read the split as a rotation rather than a broad crypto pullback. Read more 🚨 Hacks Hit Record $1.1B in H1 2026, North Korea Behind Over Half the Losses Security firm Blockaid confirmed 212 verified exploits totaling more than $1.1 billion in the first half of 2026 — already more than all of 2025 — with North Korea's Lazarus Group tied to roughly 55% of stolen funds through social engineering and multisig key compromises rather than code exploits. See details ⛏️ Celsius-Born Miner Ionic Digital Surges 26% in $2.8B Nasdaq Debut Ionic Digital, the bitcoin miner formed from Celsius Network's bankruptcy estate, jumped 26% in its Nasdaq direct listing, closing at $62.90 and giving former Celsius creditors a tradable exit for shares they received in the restructuring. The company is leaning further into AI-hosting leases alongside its bitcoin mining business. Full report 💰 Congress Renews Push to Close Crypto's $24B Wash-Sale

76662.body:
Forbes Edge

Автор: Forbes


Автор: Forbes

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/career-skill-every-professional-needs-according-jamie-e0atc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3Bzp9cZLIpQ8GdMhcrutQgHA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2RCoELpXOX2co1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~ms65kqi4~jm-null-null&eid=fz96fz-ms65kqi4-jm
  
JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is known for offering straight talk on finance and the economy, and a recent interview shows that he also applies this same candor when offering career advice for professionals.  Forbes contributor Carmine Gallo reports that in a recent conversation with Wilfred Frost for The Master Investor Podcast, Dimon offered a key piece of advice to “ambitious and hungry” professionals whose goal is to occupy senior management and leadership roles.  According to Dimon, disciplined communication is a leadership skill all employees should master, with the billionaire CEO adding that too many leaders are “sloppy” communicators. While many people view communication as a simple soft skill, the bank executive views it as a core leadership discipline that leads to faster and smarter decision-making. In fact, he calls out Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ “six-page memos” as a perfect example of how leaders can create intentional communication mechanisms in the workplace.  Gallo, author of The Bezos Blueprint, explains that Bezos previously required senior executives to replace PowerPoint presentations with carefully crafted “narratively written memos.” By substituting bullet points on a slide with written memos, individual leaders began to think and talk more clearly, sharpen their arguments before expressing them, and make better decisions more quickly. Many of Amazon’s former executives who left to start or run other companies told Gallo that the written memo was the most important management practice Bezos taught them. Read here to learn more about why Dimon loves Bezos’ executive communication exercise and why he believes all professionals should learn to utilize the rule of three when communicating their ideas.  — Courtney Connley-Hampton, Careers Staff Writer WORK SMARTER Practical insights and advice from Forbes staff and contributors to help you succeed in your job, accelerate your career and lead smarter. 76660.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Hi everyone. Ahead of today's FOMC decision, markets remain in wait-and-see mode as rate hike expectations continue to weigh on risk assets. We also take a closer look at one of the biggest structural shifts in onchain markets: the rapid rise of RFQ trading in tokenized equities. While the data suggests RFQs are taking the lead, the reality is more nuanced than the headline numbers imply.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Across the majors, this is a de-risking week with nothing green. BTC leads the drawdown, down -4.2%, followed by the Nasdaq at -4.1% and gold at -1.9%. The S&P 500 has held up best, falling just -0.7%. The cause is this afternoon's FOMC decision: hike odds have climbed back to roughly 35% from 10.7% on July 15, undoing the relief the softest consumer price index (CPI) print of 2026 delivered two weeks ago. BTC is still up 7.1% on the month compared with a -4.8% decline for the Nasdaq, so this is a give-back inside a larger move rather than a new leg lower.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dd6038d7-ee0d-4c6b-b55e-914d123eaa39/image.png?t=1785332895)
Caption: 

Tuesday itself was mixed, with DEXs the clear standout at 4.2% while BTC was little changed, gaining 0.2%. AI followed at 3.7%, crypto equities 3.4%, and Ethereum Eco 3.0%; Solana Eco was the worst of the tape at -3.5%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/df656a1d-ed2e-4175-8c11-91688e14185b/image.png?t=1785332895)
Caption: 

Four sectors are green on the week and three of them are Ethereum-related: Ethereum Eco (+5.7%), Lending (+5.7%), and DEXs (+3.5%) were positive, with Bittensor Eco (+0.9%) the outlier against AI at -3.6%. The listed-crypto complex took the worst of it as crypto miners fell -13.2%, crypto equities -8.2%, and the 2025 equity cohort -8.1%, all trading as high-beta equity against the NASDAQ's -4.1%. Privacy unwound its upgrade trade at -9.1% as ZEC fell -12.0% once Ironwood activated Tuesday at block 3,428,143, though it holds +24.3% on the month.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4d503625-5140-4ee8-ad98-b7c8409b7348/image.png?t=1785332896)
Caption:
